title: Spark-X2.6-4B adds OpenAI-compatible serving support via vLLM and SGLang
summary: The Spark-X2.6-4B release includes post-trained weights and base variants supporting OpenAI-compatible local serving via SGLang and vLLM, alongside GGUF quantizations for consumer hardware inference.
research_notes:
Download model weights or quantized variants directly from the official Hugging Face repository.

Deploy locally using llama.cpp or Ollama with the provided GGUF files for memory-constrained consumer hardware.

Serve via vLLM or SGLang to provide an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint supporting long-context requests up to 1M tokens.

Configure the thinking budget parameter (none, low, or high) per request to regulate reasoning latency and token expenditure.

Use quantized INT4 or GGUF variants when running on edge hardware or consumer GPUs to maintain low memory consumption within 4GB to 8GB.

Select the 'none' thinking budget for straightforward conversational and extractive workloads to minimize time-to-first-token, switching to 'high' for multi-step logic or code generation.

When processing long contexts up to 1M tokens, utilize paged attention runtimes like vLLM or SGLang with appropriate host memory allocations to prevent KV-cache OOM.
